title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
units.idiomatic: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

units.zh: 惠帝乃止。
units.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
units.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
units.idiomatic: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

units.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
units.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

units.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
units.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

units.zh: 由是奇之。
units.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
units.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

units.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
units.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
units.idiomatic: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

units.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
units.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

units.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
units.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
units.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

units.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
units.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
units.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

units.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
units.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
units.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

units.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
units.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
units.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

units.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
units.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
units.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

units.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
units.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

units.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
units.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
units.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

units.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
units.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

units.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
units.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
units.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

units.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
units.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
units.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

units.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
units.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
units.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

units.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
units.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
units.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

title.zh: 卷二十 志第十 禮中
title.raw: 卷二十 志第十 禮中 Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two

units.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
units.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.

units.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
units.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.

units.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。
units.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.
units.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.

title.zh: 卷七 昭帝紀
title.raw: 卷七 昭帝紀 Volume 7: Annals of Emperor Zhao

units.zh: 詔曰：「夫穀賤傷農，今三輔、太常穀減賤，其令以叔粟當今年賦。」
units.literal: Edict said: 'Grain being cheap harms farmers, now Three Adjuncts and Grand Ceremonies grain has decreased and is cheap, order to use coarse millet to substitute for this year's taxes.'
units.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'When grain prices are too low, it harms the farmers. The grain in the Three Adjuncts and the Grand Ceremonies office has become cheaper. I order that coarse millet be accepted in lieu of this year's taxes.'

units.zh: 右將軍張安世宿衛忠謹，封富平侯。
units.literal: General of the Right Zhang Anshi guarded the palace loyally and carefully, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuping.
units.idiomatic: General of the Right Zhang Anshi had served loyally and diligently in the palace guard. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuping.

units.zh: 烏桓復犯塞，遣度遼將軍范明友擊之。
units.literal: Wuhuan again violated the frontier, dispatched General Who Crosses Liaodong Fan Mingyou to attack them.
units.idiomatic: The Wuhuan again violated the frontier defenses. General Who Crosses Liaodong Fan Mingyou was dispatched to attack them.

title.zh: 卷四十七 列傳第十七 傅玄
title.raw: 卷四十七 列傳第十七 傅玄 Volume 47 Biographies 17: Fu Xuan

units.zh: 臣可無恨耳，其於觀聽，無乃有怪邪！
units.literal: Your subject may have no resentment—but for those who look and listen, is it not strange!
units.idiomatic: I can swallow the insult—but will not the world find it absurd?

units.zh: 臣識石公前在殿上脫衣，為司隸荀愷所奏，先帝不以為非，于時莫謂侵官；
units.literal: Your subject remembers when Lord Shi bared his torso in the hall, impeached by colonel director Xun Kai—the late emperor did not think it wrong; at the time none said it encroached on office;
units.idiomatic: I recall when Lord Shi stripped in the hall and Xun Kai impeached him—the late emperor approved, and no one cried ‘overreach.’

units.zh: 今臣裁糾尚書，而當有罪乎？」
units.literal: now when your subject only impeached the director of the secretariat, should there be guilt?"
units.idiomatic: Am I now to be punished for impeaching only the secretariat director?"

units.zh: 祗性至孝，早知名，以才識明練稱。
units.literal: Zhi by nature was utmost filial, early known by name, praised for talent, insight, clarity, and experience.
units.idiomatic: Deeply filial and famous early, he was admired for shrewd, seasoned ability.

units.zh: 武帝始建東宮，起家太子舍人，累遷散騎黃門郎，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin first built the eastern palace, on leaving mourning he became attendant to the heir apparent; by stages he was promoted to cavalier attendant and gentleman at the yellow gate, enfeoffed secondary marquis within the passes with three hundred households' income.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin founded the heir’s palace, Fu Zhi left mourning to become an heir’s attendant, rose to cavalier attendant and gentleman at the yellow gate, and received a secondary marquisate within the passes with three hundred households.

units.zh: 母憂去職。
units.literal: On his mother's bereavement he left office.
units.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

units.zh: 尋表兼廷尉，遷常侍、左軍將軍。
units.literal: Soon he memorialed to concurrently hold commandant of justice, was promoted to regular attendant and general of the left army.
units.idiomatic: Soon he added the post of commandant of justice, then became a regular attendant and general of the left army.

units.zh: 及帝崩，梓宮在殯，而太傅楊駿輔政，欲悅眾心，議普進封爵。
units.literal: When the emperor died, while the catalpa coffin was still in the mourning shed, grand tutor Yang Jun directed the government, wishing to please the multitude's hearts, debated universally advancing noble ranks.
units.idiomatic: While the emperor’s coffin still lay in mourning, Grand Tutor Yang Jun ran the government and proposed blanket promotions to buy popularity.

units.zh: 祗與駿書曰：「未有帝王始崩，臣下論功者也。」
units.literal: Zhi wrote to Jun: "Never yet has there been discussion of ministers' merits when an emperor has first died."
units.idiomatic: Fu Zhi wrote to Yang Jun: "No worthy court has ever handed out rewards for merit the moment an emperor dies."

title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第六十七 恩倖
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第六十七 恩倖 Volume 77 Biographies 67: Noble Favorites

units.zh: 起為建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又為舍人。
units.literal: Recalled to service as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon made Administrator of South Taishan, then again served as Confidential Adjunct.
units.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon appointed administrator of South Taishan and then again served as Confidential Adjunct.

units.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風，武帝嘗目送之，笑曰：「人生何必計門戶，紀僧真堂堂，貴人所不及也。」
units.literal: Sengzhen's bearing and speech had an elegant scholar's style. Emperor Wu once watched him depart and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."
units.idiomatic: Sengzhen's appearance and speech had an elegant scholar's bearing. Emperor Wu once watched him go and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."

units.zh: 諸權要中最被眄遇。
units.literal: Among all the powerful favorites he was most favored with attention.
units.idiomatic: Among all the powerful favorites, he was the most favored.

units.zh: 僧真子交卿，甚有解用。
units.literal: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.
units.idiomatic: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.

units.zh: 武帝崩，僧真號泣思慕。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in deep longing.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned him with deep devotion.

units.zh: 宋時道人楊法持與高帝有舊，元徽末，宣傳密謀。
units.literal: During Song, the Daoist monk Yang Fachi had old ties with Emperor Gao; at the end of Yuanhui he spread word of secret plots.
units.idiomatic: During the Song, the Daoist monk Yang Fachi had old ties with Emperor Gao. At the end of the Yuanhui era he spread word of secret plots.

value.statement: Sima Yan died in the Hanzhang hall on jiyou, in the fourth month of Taixi 1, aged fifty-five sui. He was buried at the Junyang tomb and given the temple name Shizu.

title.zh: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝
title.raw: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu

units.zh: 夏四月辛丑，以侍中車騎將軍楊駿爲太尉、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinchou, Yang Jun, palace attendant and general of chariots and cavalry, was appointed grand commandant, supervisor of all military affairs within and without, and recorder of masters-of-writing business.
units.idiomatic: Xinchou: Yang Jun took the triple portfolio—grand commandant, commander-in-chief, and chief of the secretariat.

units.zh: 己酉，帝崩于含章殿，時年五十五，葬峻陽陵，廟號世祖。
units.literal: On the day jiyou the emperor died in the Hanzhang hall at age fifty-five; he was buried at Junyang mausoleum with temple name Shizu.
units.idiomatic: Jiyou: the emperor expired in Hanzhang at fifty-five, buried at the Junyang tomb with the temple name Shizu.

units.zh: 帝宇量弘厚，造次必於仁恕；
units.literal: The emperor’s bearing was broad and his capacity magnanimous; even in haste he acted with benevolence and forgiveness.
units.idiomatic: He was large-spirited and humane even under pressure.

units.zh: 高陽許允既爲文帝所殺，允子奇爲太常丞。
units.literal: Xu Yun of Gaoyang had already been killed by emperor Wen; Yun’s son Qi served as assistant director of the grand master of ceremonies.
units.idiomatic: Xu Yun, whom Wen had executed, left a son Qi in the ritual office.

units.zh: 帝將有事於太廟，朝議以奇受害之門，不欲接近左右，請出爲長史。
units.literal: When the emperor was about to perform business in the grand temple, court discussion held that Qi came from a house that had suffered harm and should not be kept near the throne, requesting he be sent out as senior clerk.
units.idiomatic: Ministers wanted Qi barred from the rite as a victim’s son.

units.zh: 帝乃追述允夙望，稱奇之才，擢爲祠部郎，時論稱其夷曠。
units.literal: The emperor then recalled Xu Yun’s old repute, praised Qi’s talent, promoted him to director in the sacrifices bureau, and opinion of the time praised his fairness and breadth.
units.idiomatic: The emperor overruled them, praised Qi, and raised him—critics called it magnanimous.

units.zh: 平吳之後，天下乂安，遂怠於政術，耽於遊宴，寵愛后黨，親貴當權，舊臣不得專任，彝章紊廢，請謁行矣。
units.literal: After Wu was pacified, all under heaven was at peace; thereupon he slackened in governing methods, indulged in roaming feasts, doted on the empress’s kin, let close nobles hold power, no longer gave old ministers sole responsibility, canonical regulations fell into disorder, and soliciting favor became the way.
units.idiomatic: Peace bred complacency: harem kin and favorites took the reins while law grew slack.

units.zh: 既而寢疾彌留，至於大漸，佐命元勳，皆已先沒，群臣惶惑，計無所從。
units.literal: Soon he lay gravely ill; as he approached the final crisis, the founding ministers had all predeceased him, and the host of officials were frightened and at a loss.
units.idiomatic: When death neared, his great generals were gone and the court panicked.

units.zh: 會帝小差，有詔以汝南王亮輔政，又欲令朝士之有名望年少者數人佐之，楊駿祕而不宣。
units.literal: When the emperor briefly improved, an edict ordered king Liang of Runan to assist the government, and he also wished to have several young courtiers of high repute assist him, but Yang Jun suppressed the edict and did not proclaim it.
units.idiomatic: A brief rally produced orders for Sima Liang and young worthies—Yang Jun hid the edict.

units.zh: 帝復尋至迷亂，楊后輒爲詔以駿輔政，促亮進發。
units.literal: The emperor relapsed into confusion; empress Yang then forged an edict making Yang Jun regent and urging Liang to hurry to the capital.
units.idiomatic: Empress Yang forged a regency for Yang Jun.

units.zh: 帝尋小間，問汝南王來未，意欲見之，有所付託。
units.literal: The emperor briefly cleared and asked whether the king of Runan had arrived, intending to see him and entrust something.
units.idiomatic: In a lucid moment he asked for Sima Liang.

units.zh: 左右答言未至，帝遂困篤。
units.literal: Those at his side answered that he had not yet arrived, and the emperor thereupon sank into critical illness.
units.idiomatic: Told Liang had not come, he sank back into coma.

units.zh: 中朝之亂，實始於斯矣。
units.literal: The turmoil at court truly began from this.
units.idiomatic: The mid-realm disasters trace to this bedside failure.

units.zh: 制曰：武皇承基，誕膺天命，握圖御宇，敷化導民，以佚代勞，以治易亂。
units.literal: The official rescript states: The Martial Emperor received the foundation, truly bore heaven’s mandate, grasped the chart and ruled the realm, spread transformation and guided the people, replacing toil with ease and exchanging chaos for order.
units.idiomatic: The court’s summation runs thus: Emperor Wu inherited the enterprise, claimed Heaven’s charge, mastered the realm’s map, and turned exhaustion and disorder into rest and rule.

units.zh: 絕縑綸之貢，去雕琢之飾，制奢俗以變儉約，止澆風而反淳朴。
units.literal: He cut off the tribute of fine silks, removed carved and polished ornament, curbed extravagant custom toward frugality, and checked dissolute winds to return to simplicity.
units.idiomatic: He banned luxury tribute and chased the court back toward plain living.

units.zh: 是以君子防其始，聖人閑其端。
units.literal: Therefore the gentleman guards the beginning, the sage blocks the opening.
units.idiomatic: The wise seal trouble at the source.

units.zh: 而世祖惑荀勖之姦謀，迷王渾之僞策，心屢移於眾口，事不定於己圖。
units.literal: Yet Shizu was deluded by Xun Xu’s treacherous counsel, misled by Wang Hun’s false strategy, his heart repeatedly swayed by many mouths, affairs unsettled by his own deliberation.
units.idiomatic: Shizu listened to Xun Xu and Wang Hun and let rumor steer him.

units.zh: 元海當除而不除，卒令擾亂區夏；
units.literal: Yuanhai ought to have been removed and was not removed, ultimately letting him disturb the central plain;
units.idiomatic: He spared Liu Yuan and reaped rebellion;

units.zh: 子文爲沛王 李校：「宗室傳言沛王景字子文。
units.literal: Regarding “Ziwen as king of Pei,” Li’s note: “The house-of-imperial-kin biography says the prince of Pei was named Jing with style Ziwen.
units.idiomatic: For Ziwen as Prince of Pei, Li’s collation note says, "The Biographies of the Imperial Clan says that Prince Jing of Pei had the courtesy name Ziwen.

units.zh: 此舉其字者，蓋沛王名本或作『炳』及『昞』、『秉』之類，唐避世祖諱昞，於『丙』、『秉』等字皆改爲『景』。
units.literal: Here the style is given because the personal name was probably written Bing or similar characters later homogenized to Jing under Tang taboo on Bing for Shizu’s name.
units.idiomatic: The style is cited here because the Prince of Pei’s personal name was probably once written as "Bing" or with similar forms; in Tang times, to avoid the taboo on Shizu’s name Bing, graphs such as "bing" and "bing" were all changed to "Jing."

units.zh: 故紀稱其字，傳改爲『景』耳。」
units.literal: Hence the annals use his style while the biography reads Jing.”
units.idiomatic: Therefore the annals call him by his style, while the biography changes the name to Jing."

units.zh: 晉國初建，追尊曰宣王。
units.literal: When Jin state first founded posthumously honored King Xuan.
units.idiomatic: Jin raised him King Xuan.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰宣皇帝，陵曰高原，廟稱高祖。
units.literal: When Wu-di accepted abdication elevated honorific Emperor Xuan—mausoleum Gaoyuan—temple styled Gaozu.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he raised the honorific Emperor Xuan; the mausoleum was Gaoyuan; the temple name was Gaozu.

units.zh: 帝內忌而外寬，猜忌多權變。
units.literal: The Emperor inwardly jealous outwardly generous—suspicious—many stratagems.
units.idiomatic: Inside jealous—outside mild—paranoia masked.

title.zh: 卷23 漢紀十五
title.raw: 卷23 漢紀十五

units.zh: 初，冒頓破東胡，東胡餘眾散保烏桓及鮮卑山為二族，世役屬匈奴。
units.literal: Initially Modun broke the Eastern Hu; the Eastern Hu's remaining masses scattered and took refuge on Wuhuan and Xianbei mountains as two peoples, generation after generation subject to corvée and allegiance to the Xiongnu.
units.idiomatic: Initially Modun defeated the Eastern Hu; the Eastern Hu remnant peoples scattered and took refuge on the Wuhuan and Xianbei mountains as two peoples, for generations subject to corvée and allegiance to the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 武帝出破匈奴左地，因徙烏桓於上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼東塞外，為漢偵察匈奴動靜。
units.literal: Emperor Wu went out and broke the Xiongnu's left territory; he thereupon moved the Wuhuan to beyond the passes of Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Liaodong, to spy on the Xiongnu's movements for Han.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned and broke the Xiongnu's left territory, he moved the Wuhuan beyond the passes of Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Liaodong to spy on Xiongnu movements for Han.

units.zh: 置護烏桓校尉監領之，使不得與匈奴交通。
units.literal: He set a Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan to oversee and lead them, so they could not communicate with the Xiongnu.
units.idiomatic: He appointed a Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan to oversee them, so they could not communicate with the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 籍注字，故以字行。
units.literal: Household register noted the style, so he was known by the style.
units.idiomatic: The household register recorded his courtesy name, so he went by it.

units.zh: 少任氣，武帝征孫恩，季高樂從。
units.literal: In youth he was spirited; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed.
units.idiomatic: Hot-blooded in youth, he eagerly joined the campaign against Sun En.

units.zh: 及平建鄴，封新夷縣五等侯。
units.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Xinyi.
units.idiomatic: After Jiankang fell he received the fifth-rank marquisate of Xinyi.

units.zh: 盧循之難，武帝謂季高曰：「此賊行破，非卿不能破其窟穴。」
units.literal: In Lu Xun's crisis the Emperor said to Jigao, "This bandit is about to break—only you can smash his nest."
units.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's crisis the emperor told him, "This rebel is nearly finished—only you can destroy his lair."

units.zh: 即遣季高泛海襲番禺，拔之。
units.literal: He at once sent Jigao by sea to strike Panyu and took it.
units.idiomatic: He sent Jigao by sea against Panyu and captured it.

units.zh: 義熙七年，季高卒，追贈南海太守，封候官縣侯。
units.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was given Administrator of Nanhai and enfeoffed Marquis of Houguan.
units.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was made administrator of Nanhai and marquis of Houguan.

units.zh: 九年，武帝表贈交州刺史。
units.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor memorialized giving him the post of Inspector of Jiao.
units.idiomatic: the ninth year of In the emperor posthumously made him inspector of Jiao.

units.zh: 蒯恩字道恩，蘭陵承人也。
units.literal: Kuai En, styled Da'en, was a man of Cheng in Lanling.
units.idiomatic: Kuai En, courtesy name Da'en, came from Cheng in Lanling.

title.en: Volume 2, Annals 2: Emperor Jing; Emperor Wen
title.raw: 卷二 帝紀第二 世宗景帝 太祖文帝 Volume 2, Annals 2: Emperor Jing; Emperor Wen

units.zh: 冬十月丁亥，奏遣吳人相國參軍徐劭、散騎常侍水曹屬孫彧使吳，喻孫皓以平蜀之事，致馬錦等物，以示威懷。
units.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dinghai, memorialized to send Wu man Chancellor of State Army Advisor Xu Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Water Bureau Subordinate Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, informing Sun Hao of the affair of pacifying Shu, presenting horses, brocade, and such objects, in order to show awe and cherishing.
units.idiomatic: On dinghai in the tenth winter month he memorialized to send Xu Shao and Sun Yu—Wu natives in his service—to Wu with horses and brocade, to tell Sun Hao of Shu’s fall and to blend threat with kindness.

units.zh: 丙午，天子命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子。
units.literal: On bingwu, the Son of Heaven ordered Central General Who Stabilizes the Army, village marquis of Xinchang Yan, to be Jin heir apparent.
units.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.

units.zh: 二年春二月甲辰，朐䏰縣獻靈龜，歸於相府。
units.literal: Second year, spring, second month, day jiachen, Quren County presented a numinous tortoise; it was sent to the chancellor's mansion.
units.idiomatic: On jiachen in the second month of spring, the second year, Quren County sent up a sacred tortoise to the chancellor’s residence.

units.zh: 五月，天子命帝冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鐘虡宮懸，位在燕王上。
units.literal: Fifth month, the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor's crown twelve tassels, erected Son of Heaven banners and flags, going out cleared roads entering cordoned progress, riding gold-root carriage, driving six horses, prepared five-seasons secondary carriages, set up yak-tail pennants and cloud-net banners, music and dance eight rows, established bell-stands palace suspended music, rank above the Prince of Yan.
units.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor granted him the twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners, cleared roads for his comings and goings, the gold-wheeled carriage drawn by six horses, five seasonal escort chariots, yak-tail and cloud banners, eight rows of dancers, bell-chimes in the palace style, and precedence above the Prince of Yan.

units.zh: 進王妃為王后，世子為太子，王女王孫爵命之號皆如帝者之儀。
units.literal: Advanced the prince's consort to queen, heir apparent to crown prince; prince's daughters and grandsons' noble title commands all as the Son of Heaven's ritual.
units.idiomatic: His consort became queen, his heir crown prince, and the titles for his daughters and grandsons matched those of the imperial house.

units.zh: 諸禁網煩苛及法式不便於時者，帝皆奏除之。
units.literal: Various prohibitions, nets, vexing harshness, and legal models not convenient to the age—the Emperor all memorialized to remove them.
units.idiomatic: He memorialized to repeal every harsh prohibition and obsolete statute that burdened the times.

units.zh: 九月癸酉，葬崇陽陵，諡曰文王。
units.literal: Ninth month, day guiyou, buried at Chongyang Mausoleum; posthumous name King Wen.
units.idiomatic: On guiyou in the ninth month he was buried at Chongyang Mausoleum with the posthumous title Wen, the Cultured King.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，追尊號曰文皇帝，廟稱太祖。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, posthumously honored title as Emperor Wen, temple called Taizu.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Sima Zhao was posthumously raised to Emperor Wen with the temple name Taizu.

units.zh: 史臣曰：世宗以睿略創基，太祖以雄才成務。
units.literal: The history official says: Shizong by keen strategy founded the base; Taizu by heroic talent completed the task.
units.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor Shi founded the enterprise with cunning strategy, and Emperor Tai completed it with heroic force.

units.zh: 三千之士，其從如雲。
units.literal: Three thousand gentlemen—their following like clouds.
units.idiomatic: Three thousand retainers followed them like clouds.

units.zh: 世祖無外，靈關靜氛。
units.literal: Shizu without those outside; spirit passes quiet miasma.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu Sima Yan came, no foe stood beyond the pale and the sacred passes fell still.

units.zh: 反雖討賊，終為弑君。
units.literal: Although turning back punished bandits, in the end it was regicide of the lord.
units.idiomatic: Though they struck in the name of punishing traitors, in the end they slew their king.

units.zh: 魏武分沛立譙郡，魏文分汝南立弋陽郡。
units.literal: Wei Wu split Pei to establish Qiao commandery; Wei Wen split Runan to establish Yiyang commandery.
units.idiomatic: Cao Cao carved Qiao from Pei, and Cao Pi raised Yiyang from Runan.

units.zh: 及武帝受命，又分潁川立襄城郡，分汝南立汝陰郡，合陳郡于梁國。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, again split Yingchuan to establish Xiangcheng commandery, split Runan to establish Ruoyin commandery, and combined Chen commandery into Liang kingdom.
units.idiomatic: Once Sima Yan took the throne he added Xiangcheng from Yingchuan, Ruoyin from Runan, and folded Chen into Liang.

units.zh: 州統郡國十，縣八十五，戶十一萬六千七百九十六。
units.literal: The province governs ten commanderies and kingdoms, eighty-five counties, households one hundred sixteen thousand seven hundred ninety-six.
units.idiomatic: The province oversaw ten jurisdictions, eighty-five counties, and 116,796 households.

title.en: Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Yuan; Emperor Ming

units.zh: 三月，幽州刺史段末波卒，以弟牙嗣。
units.literal: In the third month Youzhou Inspector Duan Mobo died; his younger brother Ya succeeded.
units.idiomatic: The governor Duan Mobo of Youzhou died; his brother Duan Ya inherited the command.

units.zh: 戊辰，立皇子衍爲皇太子，大赦，增文武位二等，大酺三日，賜鰥寡孤獨帛，人二匹。
units.literal: On wuchen he established the imperial son Yan as imperial heir apparent, great amnesty, increased civil and military ranks two grades, great feast three days, bestowed on widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries silk, two bolts each.
units.idiomatic: On wuchen he named Sima Yan crown prince, proclaimed amnesty, raised officials two steps, feasted the realm for three days, and gave two bolts of silk to every helpless household.

units.zh: 癸巳，徵處士臨海任旭、會稽虞喜並爲博士。
units.literal: On guisi he summoned recluses Ren Xu of Linhai and Yu Xi of Kuaiji together as erudites.
units.idiomatic: On guisi he called the scholars Ren Xu and Yu Xi to court as doctors.

title.en: Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 載記第一 劉元海（劉淵） 劉宣 Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan

units.zh: 每讀《漢書》，至《蕭何》、《鄧禹傳》，未曾不反覆詠之，曰：「大丈夫若遭二祖，終不令二公獨擅美於前矣。」
units.literal: Whenever he read the Han Documents, reaching the treatises on Xiao He and Deng Yu, he never failed repeatedly to intone them, saying, "If a great husband met the two Founders, in the end he would not let the two dukes alone monopolize beauty before them."
units.idiomatic: Reading the Book of Han chapters on Xiao He and Deng Yu he would chant, "Had I served Han's founders I would not leave those two alone the laurels."

units.zh: 并州刺史王廣言之于武帝，帝召見，嘉其占對，因曰：「吾未見宣，謂廣言虛耳。
units.literal: The Governor of Bing, Wang Guang, spoke of him to Emperor Wu; the Emperor summoned and saw him, praised his answers, and therefore said, "We had not yet seen Xuan and thought Guang's words empty.
units.idiomatic: Bing governor Wang Guang praised him to Sima Yan, who interviewed Liu Xuan and said, "I thought Wang Guang exaggerated.

units.zh: 今見其進止風儀，真所謂如圭如璋，觀其性質，足能撫集本部。」
units.literal: Now seeing his advance and retreat, wind and bearing, he is truly called like jade, like fine jade; observing his nature and substance, he is sufficient to soothe and gather his native command."
units.idiomatic: Seeing his carriage I know the proverb 'like jade tablets'—he can truly pacify his people."

units.zh: 乃以宣為右部都督，特給赤幛曲蓋。
units.literal: Thereupon he made Xuan commander of the right section, specially granting red pennant and curved canopy.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yan named him right-section commander with crimson pennant and curved awning.

units.zh: 蒞官清恪，所部懷之。
units.literal: When he took office he was pure and scrupulous; those under his command cherished him.
units.idiomatic: He governed cleanly and his tribes loved him.

title.raw: 卷五十二 列傳第二十二 郤詵 阮种 華譚 Volume 52 Biographies 22: Xi Shen; Ruan Zhong; Hua Tan; Yuan Fu

units.zh: 振景觀光，俟明主而宣績。
units.literal: raising brilliance viewing glory—awaiting enlightened lord to proclaim merit.
units.idiomatic: Merit shines when an enlightened ruler appears.

units.zh: 武皇之世，天下乂安，朝廷屬意於求賢，軸有懷於幹祿。
units.literal: In Martial Emperor's age—all under Heaven peaceful—the court fixed mind on seeking worthies—linchpin bore intent on striving for salary.
units.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the realm rested—court chased talent while ministers chased posts.

units.zh: 郤詵等並韞價州裏，裒然應召，對揚天問，高步雲衢，求之前哲，亦足稱矣。
units.literal: Xi Shen and others together treasured worth in prefectures and commanderies—solemnly answered summons—responded and raised Heaven's questions—high-stepped cloud avenues—seeking among former wise—also sufficient to be praised.
units.idiomatic: Xi Shen and peers hid talent locally then answered the throne—among past worthies they deserve mention.

units.zh: 時梁祖親討劉守文於滄州，駐軍於長蘆。
units.literal: At the time the Founder was personally campaigning against Liu Shouwen at Cang Prefecture and camped his army at Changlu.
units.idiomatic: The Liang Founder was then campaigning in person against Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and had encamped at Changlu.

units.zh: 三年十二月，王師攻會，居旬日，會以潞州歸於武皇。
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army attacked Hui; within ten days Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.
units.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army besieged him; within ten days Ding Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：梁祖雄猜，疑忌功臣，忽謂敬翔曰：「吾夢丁會在前祗候，吾將乘馬欲出，圉人以馬就台，忽為丁會跨之以出，時夢中怒，叱喝數聲，因驚覺，甚惡之。」
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》 states: The Founder was fierce and suspicious and wary of meritorious commanders. Suddenly he said to Jing Xiang: "I dreamed Ding Hui was attending in front of me. I was about to mount my horse to go out when the groom brought the horse to the terrace. Suddenly Ding Hui straddled it and rode out with me. In the dream I grew angry and shouted several times, then awoke, and greatly detested it."
units.idiomatic: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》: The Liang Founder was fierce, suspicious, and wary of his great commanders. One day he suddenly told Jing Xiang, "I dreamed that Ding Hui was waiting before me as I prepared to mount and ride out. The groom led the horse to the terrace, and in the dream Ding Hui vaulted onto it and rode out with me. I shouted at him in anger several times, then woke—and the omen filled me with loathing.")

units.zh: 是月，丁會舉潞州軍民歸河東矣。）〉
units.literal: That month Ding Hui led the Luzhou army and people over to Hedong.)〉
units.idiomatic: That very month Ding Hui brought the army and people of Luzhou over to Hedong.)〉

units.zh: 引見，會泣曰：「臣非不能守潞，但以汴王篡弱唐祚，猜嫌舊將，臣雖蒙保薦之恩，而不忍相從，今所謂吐盜父之食以見王也。」
units.literal: When presented in audience Hui wept and said: "Your subject is not incapable of holding Luzhou, but because the Prince of Bian usurped and weakened the Tang succession and is suspicious of old commanders, though I received the grace of preservation I could not bear to follow him—what is now called vomiting what one's robber father fed one to show the king."
units.idiomatic: When he was received in audience Ding Hui wept and said, "It is not that I could not hold Luzhou. The Prince of Bian has usurped and enfeebled the Tang house and now suspects every old commander. Though I owed him the grace of preservation, I could not bear to follow him further. What I do now is what they call vomiting out a robber father's food to show oneself before the true king."

units.zh: 武皇納之，賜甲第於太原，位在諸將上。
units.literal: The Martial Sovereign accepted him, granted him a mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.
units.idiomatic: The Martial Sovereign welcomed him, granted him a great mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.

units.zh: 五年，汴將李思安圍潞州，以會為都招討使、檢校太尉。
units.literal: In the fifth year Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou; Hui was made chief campaign commander and acting grand commandant.
units.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, and Ding Hui was made chief campaign commander with the acting rank of Grand Commandant.

title.zh: 佞幸列傳
title.raw: 《佞幸列傳》 Biographies of Flatterers

units.zh: 孝景帝時，中無寵臣，然獨郎中令周文仁，仁寵最過庸，乃不甚篤。
units.literal: During Emperor Jing's reign, there were no inner court favorites. Only the Palace Gentleman Commander Zhou Ren enjoyed favor beyond the ordinary, but even that favor was not very deep.
units.idiomatic: During Emperor Jing's reign, there were no notable court favorites. Only Zhou Ren, the Palace Gentleman Commander, enjoyed favor somewhat beyond the ordinary, and even that was not very deep.

units.zh: 今天子中寵臣，士人則韓王孫嫣，宦者則李延年。
units.literal: Among the current emperor's inner court favorites, among gentlemen there is Han Yan, grandson of the King of Han, and among eunuchs there is Li Yannian.
units.idiomatic: Among the current emperor's favored intimates, the gentleman is Han Yan, a scion of the former Kings of Han, and the eunuch is Li Yannian.

units.zh: 嫣者，弓高侯孽孫也。
units.literal: Yan was a collateral grandson of the Marquis of Gonggao.
units.idiomatic: Han Yan was a collateral grandson of the Marquis of Gonggao.

units.zh: 今上為膠東王時，嫣與上學書相愛。
units.literal: When the current emperor was King of Jiaodong, Yan studied writing with the emperor and the two became close.
units.idiomatic: When the current emperor was still the King of Jiaodong, Yan studied writing with him, and the two grew deeply attached.

units.zh: 及上為太子，愈益親嫣。
units.literal: When the emperor became Crown Prince, he became ever more intimate with Yan.
units.idiomatic: When the emperor became Crown Prince, his intimacy with Yan only deepened.

units.zh: 嫣善騎射，善佞。
units.literal: Yan was skilled at riding and archery, and skilled at flattery.
units.idiomatic: Yan excelled at riding and archery, and was adept at the art of flattery.

units.zh: 上即位，欲事伐匈奴，而嫣先習胡兵，以故益尊貴，官至上大夫，賞賜擬於鄧通。
units.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he wished to undertake campaigns against the Xiongnu, and Yan had already practiced the arts of barbarian warfare. For this reason his rank and honor increased further, his official rank reached Senior Grand Master, and the rewards bestowed on him were comparable to those of Deng Tong.
units.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne and resolved to wage war against the Xiongnu, Yan's prior training in the military arts of the steppe peoples made him all the more valued. His rank rose to Senior Grand Master, and the gifts he received rivaled those once lavished on Deng Tong.

units.zh: 時嫣常與上臥起。
units.literal: At that time, Yan regularly shared the emperor's bed and board.
units.idiomatic: In those days, Yan shared the emperor's bed and table.

units.zh: 江都王入朝，有詔得從入獵上林中。
units.literal: The King of Jiangdu came to court, and received an edict permitting him to accompany the emperor on a hunt in the Shanglin Park.
units.idiomatic: The King of Jiangdu came to court on an audience visit and was granted an imperial edict allowing him to join the emperor's hunt in the Shanglin Park.

units.zh: 天子車駕蹕道未行，而先使嫣乘副車，從數十百騎，騖馳視獸。
units.literal: Before the emperor's chariot and procession had set out along the cleared road, he first sent Yan ahead riding in a secondary imperial chariot, attended by scores of mounted horsemen, galloping to scout the game.
units.idiomatic: Before the emperor's own chariot had even set out along the cleared road, he sent Yan ahead in a secondary imperial carriage, attended by scores of mounted riders, galloping through the park to scout the game.

units.zh: 江都王望見，以為天子，辟從者，伏謁道傍。
units.literal: The King of Jiangdu, seeing this from afar, took it for the emperor. He dismissed his attendants and prostrated himself in greeting by the roadside.
units.idiomatic: The King of Jiangdu saw this procession from a distance and, mistaking it for the emperor's own, waved his retinue aside and prostrated himself in greeting by the roadside.

units.zh: 嫣驅不見。
units.literal: Yan drove past without acknowledging him.
units.idiomatic: Yan swept past without so much as a glance.

units.zh: 太后由此嗛嫣。
units.literal: The Empress Dowager from this point bore a grudge against Yan.
units.idiomatic: From that moment, the Empress Dowager harbored a deep resentment toward Yan.

units.zh: 嫣侍上，出入永巷不禁，以姦聞皇太后。
units.literal: Yan, in his attendance upon the emperor, came and went through the Yongxiang palace women's quarters without restriction. Reports of his illicit liaisons reached the Empress Dowager.
units.idiomatic: In his attendance upon the emperor, Yan came and went freely through the Yongxiang, the palace women's quarters, without restriction. Word of his illicit affairs reached the Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 皇太后怒，使使賜嫣死。
units.literal: The Empress Dowager was furious and sent a messenger to bestow death upon Yan.
units.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was furious and dispatched a messenger to order Yan to take his own life.

units.zh: 上為謝，終不能得，嫣遂死。
units.literal: The emperor pleaded on Yan's behalf, but in the end could not obtain a pardon. Yan thereupon died.
units.idiomatic: The emperor pleaded for clemency, but the Empress Dowager would not relent, and Yan was put to death.

units.zh: 而案道侯韓說，其弟也，亦佞幸。
units.literal: The Marquis of Andao, Han Yue, was Yan's younger brother, and he too gained favor through flattery.
units.idiomatic: Han Yue, the Marquis of Andao, was Yan's younger brother, and he too became a court favorite.

units.zh: 延年坐法腐，給事狗中。
units.literal: Yannian was convicted of a crime and punished with castration, and was assigned to serve in the dog kennels.
units.idiomatic: Yannian was convicted of a crime and sentenced to castration, after which he was set to work in the palace dog kennels.

units.zh: 而平陽公主言延年女弟善舞，上見，心說之，及入永巷，而召貴延年。
units.literal: Princess Pingyang mentioned that Yannian's younger sister was skilled at dancing. The emperor saw her and was pleased. After she entered the Yongxiang palace quarters, the emperor summoned and elevated Yannian.
units.idiomatic: Princess Pingyang mentioned that Yannian's younger sister was a gifted dancer. When the emperor saw her perform, he was captivated. After she was taken into the palace, the emperor summoned Yannian and raised him to a position of honor.

units.zh: 延年善歌，為變新聲，而上方興天地祠，欲造樂詩歌弦之。
units.literal: Yannian was skilled at singing and at composing new melodies. The emperor was at that time promoting sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and wished to create musical poems and songs to be set to stringed instruments.
units.idiomatic: Yannian was a gifted singer and composer of new melodies. At that time the emperor was instituting grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and wished to commission poems and hymns to be set to music for the ceremonies.

units.zh: 延年善承意，弦次初詩。
units.literal: Yannian was skilled at anticipating the emperor's wishes, and set the newly composed poems to music in sequence.
units.idiomatic: Yannian had a gift for anticipating the emperor's wishes, and deftly set the newly composed poems to music.

units.zh: 其女弟亦幸，有子男。
units.literal: His younger sister was also favored by the emperor, and bore a son.
units.idiomatic: His younger sister likewise became an imperial favorite and bore the emperor a son.

units.zh: 延年佩二千石印，號協聲律。
units.literal: Yannian wore the seal of a two-thousand-bushel official, and held the title of Harmonizer of Tones and Pitches.
units.idiomatic: Yannian was granted the seal of a two-thousand-bushel official and bore the title Harmonizer of Tones and Pitches.

units.zh: 與上臥起，甚貴幸，埒如韓嫣也。
units.literal: He shared the emperor's bed and board, and was greatly honored and favored, on a par with Han Yan.
units.idiomatic: He shared the emperor's bed and table, honored and favored to a degree that rivaled Han Yan himself.

units.zh: 久之，寖與中人亂，出入驕恣。
units.literal: As time passed, he gradually became involved in licentious affairs with palace women, and grew arrogant and unrestrained in his comings and goings.
units.idiomatic: In time, he began carrying on illicit affairs with the palace women and grew ever more brazen and unrestrained.

title.zh: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下 Volume 23 Treatises 13: Music Part Two

units.zh: 元功配二王，芬馨世所稀。
units.literal: Prime merit paired with two kings--fragrance rare in the age.
units.idiomatic: Founding merit rivals the two kings; perfume scarce in any era.

units.zh: 我皇敘群才，洪烈何巍巍。
units.literal: Our emperor arrays throng of talents--vast merit how towering-high.
units.idiomatic: Our sovereign ranks every gift; his deed towers vast.

units.zh: 桓桓征四表，濟濟理萬機。
units.literal: Mighty he campaigns four outer regions--crowded hosts order myriad pivots.
units.idiomatic: He shakes four frontiers; dense aides thread ten thousand hinges.

units.zh: 赤烏銜書至，天命瑞周文。
units.literal: Red crow bore writing down--Heaven's mandate blessed Zhou Wen.
units.idiomatic: Crimson crows carried script; heaven blessed King Wen of Zhou.

units.zh: 神雀今來遊，為我受命君。
units.literal: Spirit finches wander here now--for our lord who received the charge.
units.idiomatic: Spirit finches roam today for our ruler who took heaven's charge.

units.zh: 嘉祥致天和，膏澤隆青雲。
units.literal: Auspicious omens bring heaven's harmony--sweet dew lifts upon cyan clouds.
units.idiomatic: Good omens marry heaven with kindness; fat dew climbs on cyan clouds.

units.zh: 退願輔聖君，與神合其靈。
units.literal: Drawing back he vows to aid holy lord--joining spirits he merges their numina.
units.idiomatic: He vows to serve the sage king and mingle souls with every god.

units.zh: 我君弘遠略，天人不足並。
units.literal: Our lord enlarges far-reaching strategy--heaven and man cannot equal him combined.
units.idiomatic: Our sovereign plots afar; heaven and earth together fall short.

units.zh: 天人初並時，昧昧何芒芒。
units.literal: When heaven and man first paired--dim dim how vast-vast.
units.idiomatic: When sky and soil first met, all was dim vast shadow.

units.zh: 逮夏禹而德衰，三代不及虞與唐。
units.literal: Down to Xia Yu virtue waned--three dynasties failed to match Yu and Tang.
units.idiomatic: By Yu of Xia virtue ebbed; three ages never matched Tang and Yu.

units.zh: 我皇盛德配堯舜，受禪即阼享天祥。
units.literal: Our emperor's flourishing virtue pairs Yao and Shun--receiving abdication he mounts the stair and tastes heaven's auspice.
units.idiomatic: Our sage equals Yao-Shun; taking abdication he mounts the stair and tastes heaven's grace.

units.zh: 率土蒙祐，靡不肅，庶事康。
units.literal: Within earth's span all receive blessing--none fail reverent; myriad matters prosper.
units.idiomatic: Soil and sky gain blessing; awe reigns; every task thrives.

title.raw: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu

units.zh: 揚州刺史應綽伐吳皖城，斬首五千級，焚穀米百八十萬斛。
units.literal: Ying Chuo, inspector of Yang province, attacked Wu’s fortress at Wan, took five thousand heads, and burned one million eight hundred thousand hu of grain and rice.
units.idiomatic: Ying Chuo stormed Wu’s Wan stronghold, counted five thousand kills, and torched nearly two million hu of enemy stores.

units.zh: 十一月辛巳，太醫司馬程據獻雉頭裘，帝以奇技異服典禮所禁，焚之於殿前。
units.literal: On the day xinsi of the eleventh month Cheng Ju, court physician, presented a pheasant-head fur robe; the emperor, because strange skills and exotic garments are forbidden by ritual canon, burned it before the hall.
units.idiomatic: Xinsi: Cheng Ju, marshal of the imperial physicians, offered a pheasant-skin cloak; the emperor burned it as illegal luxury.

units.zh: 甲申，敕內外敢有犯者罪之。
units.literal: On the day jiashen he ordered that inside and outside any who dared violate the rule be punished.
units.idiomatic: Jiashen: a decree threatened punishment for anyone peddling such finery.

title.en: Volume 67 Biographies 37: Wen Jiao; Xi Jian

units.zh: 隆曰：「我俱受二帝恩，無所偏助，惟欲守州而已。」
units.literal: Long said: "I alike received grace from two emperors—without partial aid—I only wish to guard the province.
units.idiomatic: Xi Long said, "I alike received grace from both emperors and favor neither side—I only wish to hold the province."

units.zh: 承曰：「天下者，世祖皇帝之天下也。
units.literal: Cheng said: "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.
units.idiomatic: Liu Cheng said, "The realm belongs to Emperor Wu's succession.

units.zh: 太上承代已積十年，今上取四海不平，齊王應天順時，成敗之事可見。
units.literal: Grandfather succeeding substitute already piled ten years—present emperor obtaining realm unpeaceful—Prince of Qi responds Heaven obeying season—success or defeat's matter may be seen.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui had ruled a decade; turmoil ruled the land; Prince of Qi held Heaven's mandate—the outcome was plain.

title.raw: 卷二十五 志第十五 輿服 Volume 25 Treatises 15: Travel and Dress

units.zh: 帝從其議，改青龍五年為景初元年，服色尚黃，從地正也。
units.literal: The emperor followed his proposal, changed the fifth year of Qinglong to the first year of Jingchu, honored yellow in dress colors, following the earth’s correct alignment.
units.idiomatic: The throne agreed: Qinglong year five became Jingchu year one, court color turned to yellow in deference to the “earth” alignment of the calendar.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝接天人之貺，開典午之基，受終之禮，皆如唐虞故事。
units.literal: Sima Yan, the martial founding emperor, accepted heaven’s mandate and men’s allegiance, laid the Jin dynastic base—his accession rites consciously echoed the legendary abdications of Yao and Shun.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yan, the martial founding emperor, accepted heaven’s mandate and men’s allegiance, laid the Jin dynastic base—his accession rites consciously echoed the legendary abdications of Yao and Shun.

units.zh: 晉氏金行，而服色尚赤，豈有司失其傳歟！
units.literal: The Jin house belongs to the metal phase, yet dress color honored red—could it be that the officials lost the transmission?
units.idiomatic: Jin’s element was metal, yet court dress favored red—did the ministry simply mishandle the old theory?

units.zh: 晉國既建，追尊曰景王。
units.literal: When the Jin state was established, he was posthumously honored as Prince Jing.
units.idiomatic: After the duchy of Jin was founded, he was posthumously raised to Prince Jing.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰景皇帝，陵曰峻平，廟稱世宗。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, the elevated honor title was Emperor Jing, the tomb was called Junping, the temple was called Shizong.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Sima Shi was canonized as Emperor Jing, buried at Junping, and given the temple name Shizong.

units.zh: 文皇帝諱昭，字子上，景帝之母弟也。
units.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Zhao, courtesy name Zishang, was the uterine younger brother of Emperor Jing.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s younger brother by the same mother.

units.zh: 齊人方欲任用之，敷不為之屈，遂以憂懼卒於鄴。
units.literal: The men of Qi were just then intending to employ him, but Fu would not submit to them; he thereupon died in Ye from grief and fear.
units.idiomatic: The Qi meant to win him over, but Fu would not yield and died in Ye of grief and anguish.

units.zh: 高祖平齊，贈使持節、大將軍、淮廣復三州諸軍事、三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。
units.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified Qi, he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff, Grand General, military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu three provinces, Governor of three provinces, and the posthumous name Loyal and Robust.
units.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Fu was posthumously made bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander of military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu provinces, governor of those three provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

units.zh: 葬於華陰舊塋。
units.literal: He was buried at the old family graves at Huayin.
units.idiomatic: He was buried in the family graveyard at Huayin.

units.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
units.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
units.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

translations.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.

units.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
units.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
units.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

source.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
